reason: The 32-row classical scratch proposal targets per-call scratch use in the timed n=512 path, though changing the compute body creates correctness risk and no gain is measured. The loop-control rewrite is small and preserves FP32 accumulation, but its benefit is unknown. The Strassen proposals rank lower because the measured three-buffer wrapper lost all ten paired runs; removing the output zero pass is a bounded change, while vectorizing packing may duplicate compiler optimization. Single-allocation and single-product-buffer variants retain most Strassen work. Fused transpose adds repeated A reads and substantial mapping complexity. Tail splitting does not affect the fixed n=512 timing.
